## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Curated parallels for this rule appear widely across early Buddhist monastic codes. Within the Pali tradition, direct parallels are found in the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* (pli-tv-bu-pm-sk31), the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (pli-tv-bi-vb-sk31), the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (pli-tv-bi-pm-sk31), and both the *Bhikkhu* and *Bhikkhunī Parivāra*. Outside the Pali lineage, full parallels exist in Chinese, Tibetan, and Sanskrit witnesses of the Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya (e.g., Lzh Mu Bu Vb Sk 46, xct-mu-bu-vb-sk48, and Sanskrit Prātimokṣa manuscripts) and an Upāliparipṛcchā translation. Resembling regulations on respectful receipt and consumption of almsfood (*Sakkaccapaṭiggahaṇa*) are found in the Sarvāstivāda, Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, and Mahāsāṅghika traditions.

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog data.*
